summary: The candidate captures the paper's full internal mathematical spine with generally faithful formulas and appropriate definition/theorem/lemma typing. All principal gluing, self-gluing, trisection, and three-manifold results have recognizable counterparts. Its main defects are failure to extract most external background results as attributed claims, several duplicated entries caused by overlapping chunks, inconsistent IDs and theorem-number metadata, and some page-locator discrepancies. A few statements also omit qualifiers such as the grading in Lemma 3.7.
strengths: All central internal results are represented: Lemma 3.7, Theorems 3.8, 3.14, and 3.15, the trisection formula, Lemma 4.5, and Theorem 4.7.
The foundational categories, cornered four-manifold bimodule, bimodule tensor product, zero-th Hochschild homology, trisection data, and surface skein bicategory are covered.
Most formulas, hypotheses, quotient relations, and module or bimodule targets are mathematically faithful and have balanced LaTeX delimiters.
Definitions, lemmas, and theorems are generally assigned suitable entry types.
Several useful supporting definitions beyond the minimum gold set are extracted, including the relation sim3 and the three-manifold bicategory modules.
issues: The Banyaga fragmentation lemma is entirely absent as an externally attributed background result.
The Gay-Kirby entry records only their definition of a trisection, omitting the gold claim about existence and stable uniqueness.
The Morrison-Walker-Wedrich foundation and Ren-Willis gluing result appear only indirectly as unattributed definitions or calculations; the Ren-Willis surjectivity claim is not preserved.
Chunk overlap creates substantial duplication, including the cornered bimodule, Theorem 3.8, the trisection definition, Theorem 3.15, Lemma 4.5, and the three-manifold module tensor product.
Entry IDs and numbering are inconsistent: equivalent results use different namespaces and some formal theorem numbers are omitted.
One duplicate of Theorem 3.8 is assigned page 2 rather than the gold formal locator on page 9; Theorem 3.15 and several later definitions also differ from the gold page locators.
The Lemma 3.7 statement omits the gold statement's explicit graded-module qualifier.
Corollary 3.19 is labeled as a theorem rather than explicitly retained as a corollary.

entryLevelComparison.note: Objects, morphism skein module, boundary data, and composition are faithfully captured on page 4.
The bifunctor and object values are accurate, but the same definition is extracted twice.
The direct sum and balancing relation sim1 are preserved.
The diagonal direct sum and cyclic relation sim2 are correctly stated.
The manifold decomposition and diagram conditions are split into separate entries; the trisection definition is also duplicated.
Objects, 1-cells, and skein-lasagna 2-cells are accurately represented, though the candidate locator is page 15 rather than gold page 14.
The foundational construction is captured, but not as an externally attributed Morrison-Walker-Wedrich result.
The gluing map is present, but external attribution and the asserted surjectivity are missing.
No entry records the externally cited fragmentation lemma.
Gay and Kirby are named as the source of the definition, but existence and stable uniqueness are omitted.
The map, quotient, and isomorphism are correct; the explicit graded-module qualifier is dropped.
The bimodule isomorphism is accurate, but appears three times; one occurrence has the incorrect formal locator page 2.
The intermediate self-gluing evaluation isomorphism is faithfully represented.
The isotopy-invariance statement is correct and appears twice.
The Hochschild-homology self-gluing formula, hypotheses, and grading are preserved.
The quotient by sim3 and recovery of the closed-manifold module are accurate, but duplicated and assigned page 13 rather than gold page 12.
The full three-sector Hochschild formula is accurate, but the corollary is labeled as a theorem and its page differs from the gold locator.
The boundary hypotheses and categorical tensor-product gluing formula are faithfully stated with the correct theorem number and page.
